editorial:
Imagine a dying town in Ohio where the air feels thick and something mean is hiding in the dark. You follow Lamont, a guy just trying to run his diner after a tragedy, who meets a grizzled monster hunter named Belko. The chemistry between these two is great because you have a scared local paired with a man who has seen everything. It feels like a gritty road trip movie but with fangs and blood. The vibe is dark and moody, making you feel like you are right there in the rain and rust of Redpatch.

What really makes this work are the fight scenes, which are punchy and fast. The pacing never slows down, though a few plot points feel a bit rushed. If you love monsters and tough-guy dialogue, you will have a blast. For the best experience, you should definitely stream this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the detail in the makeup. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move because the colors look amazing on a big screen.
endingExplained: In the final fight, you find out the ancient evil was actually using the town's mayor as a puppet. Lamont has to step up and use a silver stake to kill the main vampire while Belko holds off the minions. Once the boss dies, the other monsters turn to dust instantly. Lamont finally finds peace with his father's death and decides to keep training with Belko to hunt more monsters.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves monster hunts and small town mysteries.
